newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Republic opens busy week.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Republic opens busy week.

text.p: The Republic of Brazil launched its 150 million sterling bond on Monday to kick off what looks set to be a fairly active week in the Eurobond market for Brazilian issuers.
The 10-year bond was led by BZW and CS First Boston and came at a spread of 275 basis points over U.K. gilts, as the market had anticipated.
It widened about five basis points after launch, traders said.
The deal lent support to the Central Bank's claim that it was not worried by an Italian court ruling last month in favor of creditors of a now defunt coffee institute.

The court ruled that Brazilian sovereign Eurobond funds raised in Italy could be seized to repay the creditors. No money was ever seized and the matter must still be cleared up in the courts. Central Bank officials say they doubt the ruling will ever be enforced.
Still, there was talk in the market last week that the bank was indefinitely delaying the sterling issue, fearing an English court was about to issue a similar ruling.
The Central Bank denied the talk and said the bond was being delayed because of last week's Bank of England interest rate hike.
OTHER NEW ISSUES EXPECTED THIS WEEK include deals from a wide variety of sectors.

* Construction firm Camargo Correa may bring its $150 million eight-year bond, with puts and calls at five years, to market. Chase is leading the deal which was expected to price at a spread of 200-240 bp to the five-year put.

* Private power firm Escelsa, which once belonged to the state of Espirito Santo, was expected to price its $350 million 10-year bond through Morgan Stanley. Price talk is at 330-350 bp over U.S. Treasuries.
* Brazil Realty's $60 million eight-year bond, with puts and calls at five years, could price this week via Bear Stearns, debt watchers said.
TRADER TIP: OUT OT THE OLD, INTO THE NEW

In secondary trade, spreads on older issues have tightened while spreads on new issues have widened by about 20 basis points over the past two weeks. This has made a number of new issues more attractive, traders said.

"Clients are just stuffed with new paper but I don't see spreads on new issues getting any wider. This is a good time to switch out of old issues and into new issues," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.

Among the new issues to consider are steel firm CSN's 9.125 percent due 2007 ZYJJ, which priced at a spread of 275 bp and is now trading at about 300 bp over. Sao Paulo power firm Cesp's 9.125 percent due 2007 (call 02) ZYGZ, which is trading at 295 bp, up from a launch price of 285, also looks like a buy, traders said.
By comparison, Minas Gerais power company Cemig's 9.125 percent due 2004 (put 01) ZQRO, which was issued in November last year, has tightened 25 bp to 215 bp over during the last two weeks.
